title: One slow product blocks the shop
scenario: Desk Lamp, Task Chair and Writing Desk share two Storefront workers. Only the lamp’s Inventory network branch becomes slow. Repeated lamp requests hold the workers; healthy chair and desk requests now queue or are rejected. The complete catalog also waits for the lamp result.
why: The mitigation now protects other products. A 400 ms timeout releases a worker, the 5-second circuit breaker stops repeated waiting on the lamp, and the fallback lets the catalog show chair and desk while lamp stock is unconfirmed. These are three different mechanisms; fallback alone does not free capacity.
reproduce: Choose Inventory in Network Faults and apply a 1500 ms response delay. It affects only Desk Lamp’s branch. Use “Refresh all availability” in Storefront and watch the fixed background traffic fill the two shared workers.
ready: Start with “Clear all faults” and “Restore default settings” in Network Faults. Use the start launcher so fixed background traffic is running. In Storefront, compare the three-product catalog and its worker indicators. Keep the same traffic throughout, use fresh 60–90-second windows, and record changes in the cumulative rejected count rather than its lifetime total.
assignment: Can you keep the healthy chair and desk available while temporarily disabling an unconfirmed lamp availability check?

tasks.title: Measure the healthy catalog
tasks.instruction: Use “Refresh all availability”. Record all three stock results, catalog time, workers, queue size and the starting rejected count. In Grafana inspect “Product p95 latency” and “Shared workers and queue”. Predict which products can be affected despite having healthy dependency branches; state an abort condition.

tasks.title: Create a lamp-only slowdown
tasks.instruction: Apply +1500 ms to Inventory in Network Faults. Keep supplied traffic unchanged and refresh the catalog. Record lamp delay, chair/desk queue time or failures, catalog status, and the change in rejected requests over a fresh window. The slow request consumes actual shared workers; the indicators are measured state.

tasks.title: Trace the propagation
tasks.instruction: Compare “Dependency p95 latency”, “Product p95 latency”, “Shared workers and queue”, and “Capacity rejection rate”. Explain the path: lamp Inventory delay → occupied workers → healthy products waiting/rejected, plus the catalog waiting for every product. A queue can fluctuate; use a full window.

tasks.title: Apply containment
tasks.instruction: Remove the fault first. Open Fallbacks & timeouts and use Challenge 1 settings. This applies a 400 ms Inventory timeout and enables fallback plus the product/dependency circuit breaker. Predict the distinct effect of each mechanism.

tasks.title: Repeat the same fault and verify recovery
tasks.instruction: Reapply the identical +1500 ms Inventory delay. Refresh several times, including within and after a 5-second cooldown. Compare chair/desk live results, queue pressure, rejection-rate changes, catalog latency, and lamp stock uncertainty. The lamp availability action should be disabled while stock is unconfirmed. Clear all faults, restore default settings, wait for in-flight work and any 5-second cooldown, then verify all three products have live stock and delivery information. Submit your own measurements.

done: You measured healthy, delayed and mitigated phases under unchanged traffic.
You observed and explained impact on chair/desk or the complete catalog, then verified that impact shrank while lamp stock remained unconfirmed.
You distinguished timeout, circuit breaker and fallback; compared equal windows; and verified cleanup.
solution: Healthy: all three product branches answer quickly and the complete catalog is live. Record actual local timings.

With +1500 ms on the lamp Inventory branch, repeated lamp requests can exceed two workers of capacity. Chair/desk requests wait or are rejected even though their own dependency paths are healthy. A complete catalog also waits for or fails on one missing result.

With a 400 ms timeout, a failed lamp call releases its worker sooner. The circuit breaker then skips that product/dependency path for 5 seconds; the fallback returns unknown stock instead of rejecting the entire catalog. Chair and desk can return live information.
Expect a probe and possible short latency spike every cooldown while the fault persists. HTTP 200 is not confirmed lamp stock. Remove the fault and restore defaults; verify all three recover.

fields.label: Healthy baseline and metric
fields.prompt: Which route and metric did you choose? Include your measured baseline. Include all three products, complete-catalog timing/status, worker queue and rejected-count change over the same observation window.

fields.label: Hypothesis and abort condition
fields.prompt: What did you expect from +1500 ms Inventory latency, and when would you stop?

fields.label: Fault evidence
fields.prompt: Record the same route under fault: latency, success rate, Inventory signal, and time window. Include all three products, complete-catalog timing/status, worker queue and rejected-count change over the same observation window.

fields.label: Mitigation and reason
fields.prompt: What timeout/fallback did you use, and why is it safe for a product page? Distinguish the roles of timeout, circuit breaker and fallback.

fields.label: Same-fault validation
fields.prompt: What happened when you applied the identical fault after mitigation? Include all three products, complete-catalog timing/status, worker queue and rejected-count change over the same observation window.

fields.label: Conclusion and cleanup
fields.prompt: Did resilience improve? What information is now uncertain? Confirm that the fault was removed.

overview.title: 1 · A slow lamp blocks healthy products
overview.description: Watch shared workers fill, then protect chair and desk with bounded waiting and honest partial results.

mitigationHelp.description: Use the built-in 400 ms timeout, fallback and 5-second per-product/dependency circuit breaker. Under the same delay the lamp becomes unconfirmed; chair and desk should stay live.
mitigationHelp.instruction: In Network Faults → Fallbacks & timeouts, click “Use Challenge 1 settings”. Repeat the same fault and watch the catalog, queue and product latency.
